Title: The root and real homepage are split across two indexable URLs
Current: The root is a generic Blog archive; /home/ is a separate branded, self-canonical page. Navigation and search signals split brand and conversion intent.
Fix: Make the branded experience the root; move the archive to /blog/; 301 /home/ to /; align canonicals, social URLs, schema, breadcrumbs, menus, internal links, and sitemaps.

Title: Blog pagination is broken and repeats page one
Current: Pages 2â€“8 return 200 but repeat page-one headings, show current page 1, use generic title Blog, and canonicalize to the root; older sitemap posts are not exposed by the visible pager.
Fix: Repair the WordPress paged query and complete crawlable pagination on the surviving archive. Give real page sets differentiated titles and correct canonicals; consolidate redundant variants only after coverage is proven.

Title: Eight demo records are indexed as real people, testimonials, and cases
Current: Eight sitemap-listed, indexable, self-canonical records reuse Latin-like theme-demo copy and placeholder identities; the deterministic crawl also groups them into duplicate-content/description clusters.
Fix: Unpublish; return 410 where approved; remove from sitemaps and internal links. Only publish permissioned, substantiated identities/cases with dates, scope, methods, outcomes, and disclosure.

Title: The newsletter conversion system is visibly broken
Current: The footer and /newsletter/ expose raw malformed MailPoet shortcodes; /newsletter-2/ is a duplicate indexable route with an unresolved legal token.
Fix: Repair shortcode/plugin configuration; consolidate newsletter routes; state promise, cadence, consent, privacy, and unsubscribe expectations; then prove confirmation and delivery end to end.

Title: High-stakes career guidance contains mislabeled, retired, or unsupported credentials
Current: The page misnames or mislinks Google, AWS, Databricks, OpenAI Gym, and NVIDIA credentials and omits verification date, exact code/status, costs, prerequisites, renewal, role, and selection method.
Fix: Temporarily remove from the index; rebuild only from issuer primary sources with verified-on date, exact credential/code/status, fees, prerequisites, renewal, intended role, limitations, and methodology.

Title: Foundational AI explainers contain basic factual errors
Current: The page incorrectly frames GPT-3 as the original GPT, states GPT-J has 178B parameters, attributes Megatron-Turing NLG to Google, and uses unqualified AGI language.
Fix: Retract pending review, then replace with a versioned primary-source timeline distinguishing model families, products, release dates, parameter counts, availability, provenance, capabilities, and limitations.

Title: The Grok article appears to invent or conflate a business platform
Current: The article describes an unidentified custom-model platform with enterprise, integration, security, support, and setup-team claims without vendor identity or supporting product evidence. The report explicitly labels conflation/fabrication as an inference, not proven intent.
Fix: Remove pending verification. If the subject is xAI Grok, rewrite solely from dated primary product material and do not infer unsupported enterprise/security capabilities.

Title: There is no accountable author behind 71 posts
Current: All 71 posts use the domain-named account; the biography/avatar are generic; Person schema uses the domain; institutional and reviewer responsibility is not supported visibly.
Fix: Assign real accountable individual bylines and qualification-specific bios; publish reviewed-by, dates, source/correction/editorial/AI-use/conflict/affiliate policies, legal publisher, and correction history.

Title: Public runtime is obsolete and version details are exposed
Current: Captured responses advertise PHP/8.1.34, an end-of-life branch. Generator tags and asset query strings advertise WordPress/plugin versions, but those strings are not an authenticated installed-package inventory.
Fix: Back up and stage-test; move to a supported PHP branch; update WordPress/theme/plugins after compatibility testing; remove unused extensions; enable managed security updates; suppress unnecessary disclosure.

Title: Internal links contain two 404s and sitewide redirect waste
Current: Two malformed/missing link targets were confirmed; 36 unique internal destinations redirect; apex/index.php Blog, Home, and Contact links recur roughly 228â€“229 times across the snapshot.
Fix: Replace internal anchors with final HTTPS www URLs; fix the two 404 destinations; eliminate /index.php and apex variants at the template/menu source.

Title: Mobile payloads are excessive
Current: At 390Ã—844, / transferred about 11.95 MB (11.21 MB images) and /home/ about 34.48 MB. Oversized originals, duplicate variants, 27 images, 24 scripts, and several 1.7â€“2.3 MB images were observed. Load-event timings are lab observations, not field CWV.
Fix: Generate responsive AVIF/WebP; configure srcset/sizes; stop serving originals as cards; preload only actual LCP; lazy-load below-fold assets; remove duplicate carousel assets; reduce scripts and DOM.

Title: Metadata control is poor across the sitemap inventory
Current: The deterministic 114-URL audit found 6 generic titles, 38 titles over 60, 38 under 20, 12 missing descriptions, 50 over 160, 13 under 70, 2 duplicate-title groups, and 1 duplicate-description group. Thresholds are snippet heuristics, not ranking penalties.
Fix: Write intent-specific title/description templates; remove keyword dumps/article-length descriptions; consolidate duplicate routes; make archives unique.

Title: Headings and thin hubs fail page intent
Current: The deterministic audit found 1 page missing H1, 3 pages with multiple/blank H1s, and 29 pages under 300 main-content words. About Us has a giant H2; near-empty hubs and visible â€œService Urlâ€ text were also observed.
Fix: Use one descriptive H1 and coherent H2/H3 hierarchy; remove blank/misleveled headings; enrich pages that serve a real task and redirect/noindex/retire pages that do not.

Title: Front-end errors and broken components occur sitewide
Current: Rendered pages repeatedly log ReferenceError: wp is not defined. Sitewide defects also include raw MailPoet output, tel:contact@aiamigos.org, an HTTP YouTube URL, stale @2023 copyright, and misleading theme attribution.
Fix: Correct dependency enqueueing or remove the orphaned call; fix shortcode, email and HTTP schemes, attribution, and dynamic copyright.

Title: Brand and audience are incoherent
Current: The site simultaneously targets children, parents, students, career switchers, engineers, enterprise buyers, consultants, shoppers, and newsletter readers under multiple product/brand names without one primary promise.
Fix: Approve one primary audience, business model, and promise; segment materially different propositions with named owners, evidence, journeys, and editorial standards.

Title: Childrenâ€™s content makes unsupported safety promises
Current: Childrenâ€™s pages omit age bands, supervision/account requirements, privacy/data review, moderation/community risk, ads, accessibility, learning objectives, and review dates while using absolute safe/educational wording without a documented method.
Fix: Add educator/parent review, age and supervision bands, privacy/ads checks, known risks, accessibility, learning goals, test dates, and off-domain disclosure; remove unsupported absolutes; obtain child/privacy legal review.

Title: Affiliate-style book recommendations lack disclosure and method
Current: The page labels four books â€œbestâ€ in about 147 words, uses amzn.to links, and lacks exact edition metadata, age/reading method, comparison criteria, testing evidence, limitations, price context, and affiliate disclosure.
Fix: Disclose relationships prominently; publish selection/comparison method; identify author/edition/ISBN and age/reading level; add strengths/weaknesses and descriptive links; remove â€œbestâ€ absent evidence.

Title: About, mission, and service claims lack evidence
Current: About and service copy claims courses, tools, hands-on experience, community, premier/renowned status, and international events without named owners, methods, outcomes, customers, curriculum, metrics, or event records. Mission uses a meaningless slug, inconsistent singular brand, and stray punctuation.
Fix: Replace unsupported adjectives with legal/operator identity, named qualified owners, methodology, verified metrics, event/case records, correction process, and contact details; correct route/name/punctuation.

Title: Privacy copy does not match site activities
Current: The privacy page is largely default WordPress language and does not adequately cover controller/operator, effective date, newsletter processing, attachments, analytics/social embeds, affiliate short links, child-directed content, vendors, or realistic retention. This is a trust/content mismatch, not a legal conclusion.
Fix: Obtain legal review and publish activity-specific privacy, cookies, child-safety, affiliate, vendor, processing, and retention disclosures adjacent to relevant collection points.

Title: Content and archive clusters overlap without an intent map
Current: Fourteen additional self-canonical indexable archive URLs outside the sitemap overlap with root/category/author archives. About/Mission, newsletter, introductory AI, career, prompting, and Generative AI pages overlap. Actual query cannibalization requires Search Console evidence.
Fix: Create an intent map with one canonical owner per intent; merge/redirect variants; distinguish surviving support pages by job-to-be-done; validate query effects with Search Console when authorized.

Title: Roadmap, test, and benchmark headlines do not deliver reproducible artifacts
Current: Four headline-led articles omit promised architecture/code/evaluation/cost/deployment artifacts or use unfinished instructions, arbitrary targets, or qualitative scores without models, datasets, prompts, methods, outputs, or uncertainty.
Fix: Either retitle each as an editorial overview or publish executable/reproducible artifacts with versioned source, fixtures, methods, outputs, acceptance criteria, limitations, and correction history.

Title: Social cards are incomplete
Current: The deterministic crawl found 25 sitemap pages without an OG image and 11 without a Twitter description; broader rendered sampling found additional incomplete core fields.
Fix: Provide an approved 1200Ã—630 default and complete title, description, URL, image, and card fields on every indexable template.

Title: Image alt text requires a human relevance review
Current: No captured image lacked the alt attribute, but 184 image elements had empty alt on 77 pages. Empty alt may be correct for decoration, so this is a review queue rather than 184 proven violations.
Fix: Classify each empty-alt instance as decorative or informative/functional; retain empty alt only for decoration, add concise contextual alt where required, and remove redundant linked copies.

Title: Schema is syntactically healthy but semantically uneven
Current: All sitemap pages exposed parseable JSON-LD with no JSON errors, but demo records have weak semantics, root/archive entity choices are uneven, Person uses a domain string, and EducationalOrganization lacks visible support.
Fix: Model only substantiated Organization, Person, Article, CollectionPage, and related entities; align structured data with visible content; never add Review markup to unverifiable testimonials.

Title: Mixed-scheme references remain
Current: All 114 sitemap pages contain at least one HTTP link because the footer YouTube target is global; eight unique HTTP targets were observed. upgrade-insecure-requests masks rather than removes the debt.
Fix: Change every TLS-capable reference and resource to explicit HTTPS; remove or document any unavoidable non-TLS destination.

Title: Mobile controls are undersized or unlabeled despite no basic horizontal overflow
Current: At 390Ã—844, root and /home/ did not overflow and the menu opened, but social targets were about 17px high, menu rows about 39px, 20 carousel controls lacked accessible names, and /home/ rendered ~1,062 DOM elements with repeated carousel content in the accessibility tree.
Fix: Target approximately 44Ã—44 CSS pixels, label every control, hide cloned slides from assistive technology, and reduce DOM/carousel duplication.

Title: Response hardening and caching headers are weak
Current: Audited HTML lacked HSTS, nosniff, frame protection, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, and explicit HTML Cache-Control; CSP only requested upgrade-insecure-requests and versions were disclosed. These are hygiene issues, not direct ranking factors.
Fix: Approve and deploy appropriate HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors/frame protection, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, CSP, and explicit HTML caching rules; validate compatibility in staging.

Title: Formulaic AI-content language weakens authority
Current: Across 71 posts, repeated stock phrases and hype-oriented headlines are frequent. Publication patterns resemble mass-produced content, but this does not prove AI authorship or a search penalty.
Fix: Rewrite priority pages around a defined reader problem, scope, evidence/test, result, limitations, and accountable authorship; remove stock enthusiasm and unsupported superlatives.

Title: Grammar and production defects are recurrent
Current: The snapshot contains recurrent spelling, punctuation, placeholder, heading/list, numbering, and label defects across templates and content.
Fix: Adopt a human prepublication checklist and automated regression scans for grammar, headings, links, placeholders, factual sources, brand form, and headline fulfillment.

Title: Taxonomy has no visible editorial strategy
Current: 61 of 71 posts sit in generic Blog whose description is â€œYour blog categoryâ€; several indexable categories contain only 1â€“5 posts; a public taxonomy label misspells College.
Fix: Reduce taxonomy to approved user journeys; merge micro-categories; write useful archive introductions; noindex archives until they independently serve intent.

Title: Contact conversion asks for data without explaining the exchange
Current: The page says Sign up today, requests phone, permits uploads, and omits clear purpose, necessity, attachment rules, recipient, retention, response time, and local privacy context.
Fix: Name the actual action, minimize fields, state purpose/response time/attachment rules/recipient/retention, and place relevant privacy notice before submission.

Title: Publication freshness is weak for a fast-moving AI site
Current: Of 71 posts, 58 date to 2023, 11 to 2024, two to 2025, and none to 2026 at audit time; 28 have no external references, 22 are under 600 words, and 12 have no content headings. Bursts alone do not prove automation or penalty.
Fix: Triage every post: update with primary sources and visible reviewed-on/reviewer, merge, noindex, or retire. Favor fewer tested source-rich updates over bulk publication.

Title: Public WordPress registration was enabled alongside a large unreviewed Subscriber population
Current: Authenticated production observation on 2026-08-13: WordPress Settings > General had 'Anyone can register' enabled. The Users inventory showed 294 total accounts: 1 Administrator and 293 Subscribers. Sampled Subscriber rows were dominated by scam-, crypto-, casino-, or spam-themed identities; sampling does not prove that all 293 Subscriber accounts are malicious. The authorized operator disabled public registration in production and verified after reload that users_can_register=false. Subscriber review, quarantine, and cleanup have not been completed or claimed.
Fix: Keep public registration disabled, preserve and export the full user inventory, define an approved allowlist and account-classification policy, create and verify a recoverable backup, then conduct an evidence-preserving account review. Quarantine only accounts supported by approved evidence and retain an auditable disposition for every reviewed account; do not bulk-delete or label all Subscribers malicious from the sample.
